security_feature_bypassed: The reporting of an illegal or unimplemented HMAC command. src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:428 ties the illegal-command status error2_sts.hwset to constant 1'b0 with a TODO comment, while its siblings at :426-427 are driven from real logic. Combined with the absence of the finalization command from the RTL, a finalization request written to HMAC512_CTRL is neither performed nor reported.
finding: The HMAC final-block command is absent end to end: src/hmac/rtl/hmac_core.sv:24-44 declares init_cmd and next_cmd but no finalization input, and the identifier last_cmd occurs nowhere in src/hmac/rtl or src/hmac_drbg/rtl. src/hmac/rtl/hmac_reg.sv:868-888 nevertheless gives HMAC512_CTRL bit 5 a real flop and exports it to the wrapper, where src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:257-260,304 consumes only INIT, NEXT, ZEROIZE, MODE and CSR_MODE and never reads it. The write is therefore accepted and retained but drives nothing. Because src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:428 holds error2_sts at zero, and because the two error conditions that are driven both conjoin kv_key_data_present at :395-396, no register-programmed command can raise any error. A finalization request is absorbed silently: STATUS.VALID never rises, the tag does not change, and no status bit reports the command as illegal. HMAC512_CTRL is software-write-only, so the request cannot be read back either.

location_or_code_reference.attachment_note: A witness testbench, simulation script, structural audit and negative control are attached. The testbench drives one whole hmac block over its native cs/we register port only, with no force, no deposit and no hierarchical assignment into the DUT, and runs each configuration from its own reset.

detection_method: The command decode was read against the register description, and the field the specification assigns to final-block signalling was traced forward to its consumers. The trace terminated: the field has storage and is exported, but nothing in the wrapper reads it. The interrupt drivers were then read as a group, which exposed that the one status provisioned to report an illegal command is tied to a constant while its siblings are driven. Both observations were turned into scripted structural gates and then into a directed register-bus simulation that issues the command and observes STATUS, the tag registers and the error interrupt status.
security_impact: Software issuing a message finalization request to the HMAC block receives no error, no completion and no readback, so it cannot distinguish a performed finalization from a discarded one. A caller that treats the absence of an error as success will proceed on a tag that was never computed for the finalized message. The absent illegal-command reporting is the part that makes this durable rather than merely incomplete: because the only two driven error conditions require a KeyVault sideload, a register-programmed command can never be reported as invalid, so no amount of defensive polling by software can detect the condition.
proposed_mitigation: Restore the final-block command in the register block, the wrapper and the core: give hmac_core.sv a finalization input alongside init_cmd and next_cmd, consume the HMAC512_CTRL field in hmac.sv next to the existing INIT and NEXT terms at :257-258, and route it into the core FSM so the final block's padding and length handling is performed as docs/CaliptraHardwareSpecification.md:1129,1134 requires.
Restore the corresponding command in the DRBG call chain, so the K, V and T final HMAC operations request finalization rather than issuing only non-final blocks.

Drive the illegal-command status at src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:428 from real logic instead of 1'b0, so any command the block cannot honour is reported through error_internal_intr_r bit 2 rather than absorbed. The same applies to error3_sts at :429.

Apply the swwe readiness qualifier to the finalization field as hmac.sv:251 does for INIT, and give it the singlepulse property its command siblings carry, so a request cannot be accepted while the block is busy and cannot persist as a stale command after the write.
If the field is genuinely intended to remain reserved, make writes to it raise the illegal-command status rather than latch silently, so software learns its request was not accepted.

cvss_v3_1.scoring_note: Scored with the CVSS v3.1 calculator from the impact that was measured, not the impact the missing protocol could be argued to enable. What was demonstrated is that a command is silently discarded and cannot be detected as such, which is an integrity-relevant defect in the command interface: I:L. No confidentiality loss was shown, since the witness reads back only its own material, and the block remains available and responsive throughout, so C:N and A:N. Local register access at the privilege that reaches the block's window gives AV:L, AC:L, PR:L.

exploit_or_attack_flow: Software programs the sixteen HMAC512_KEY words and the thirty-two HMAC512_BLOCK words over the ordinary register interface. No KeyVault sideload is used, so kv_key_data_present is low and neither driven error condition can arm.
Software writes HMAC512_CTRL with only bit 5 set, requesting message finalization. The register block accepts the write, latches it into the flop at hmac_reg.sv:885, and exports it to the wrapper.
The wrapper never reads the field, so no command reaches the core. STATUS.READY remains set and STATUS.VALID never rises.
Software polls HMAC512_STATUS and reads error_internal_intr_r. Both report nothing: no completion, and no illegal-command status, because error2_sts.hwset is tied to zero at hmac.sv:428.

Software cannot read HMAC512_CTRL back to check what it requested, because the register is software-write-only at hmac_reg.rdl:68. Having observed no error, a caller that treats silence as success consumes the tag registers as though the message had been finalized, when no operation ran at all.
